hadronic freeze-out in heavy-ion collisions is a well defined physical observable which can be employed to determine the QCD transition boundary at non-zero net baryon densities.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the freeze-out line in the (μ B, T) plane is not a unique function of the collision energy, but rather depends strongly on the hadron multiplicity established at hadron formation.
the freeze-out line of the hadron/resonances coincides with the parton-hhadron transition line, which is a consequence of the UrQMD model description of the hadronization process.
the freeze-out points of the hadron multiplicites in heavy-ion collisions are not affected by the hadronic rescattering phase, but rather represent the conditions at the end of the partonic phase.
